Audit grades from a vitals task

Source: R/integrations.R
audit_vitals.Rd

Extracts samples from a vitals::Task, joins blind human labels, and delegates to calibrate_judge(). No model is called by this adapter.

Usage

audit_vitals(
  task,
  human_labels,
  id_col = "id",
  human_col = "human_label",
  score_col = "score",
  provenance = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

task

A vitals::Task-like object with a get_samples() method, or a samples data frame for testing/offline use.

human_labels

A label vector aligned with samples, or a data frame keyed by id_col and containing human_col.

id_col

Unique sample ID column.

human_col

Human-label column name.

score_col

Vitals score column containing judge grades.

provenance

Optional audit metadata merged with adapter metadata.

...

Additional arguments passed to calibrate_judge().

Value

A yourhonor_calibration object.

Repeated epochs

A vitals task with multiple epochs contains duplicated item IDs. This adapter deliberately rejects those rows for calibration because treating reruns as independent gold items would make confidence intervals too narrow. Filter to one epoch before calling audit_vitals(). Use stability_vitals() for epochs only when every judge-visible content field is invariant within item.

Examples

# A samples data frame stands in for a vitals task here; with vitals
# installed, pass the task itself and its `get_samples()` is read.
samples <- tibble::tibble(
  id = paste0("q", 1:8),
  input = paste("question", 1:8),
  score = c("C", "C", "P", "I", "C", "P", "I", "C")
)
# Human labels keyed by sample ID, in any order.
human <- tibble::tibble(
  id = paste0("q", 8:1),
  human_label = c("C", "I", "C", "C", "I", "P", "C", "C")
)
cal <- audit_vitals(samples, human, label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
                    n_boot = 200, seed = 1)
cal
#> 
#> ── yourhonor judge calibration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 8 usable items of 8 - descriptive judge-vs-human agreement:
#> • cohen_kappa: 0.79 [0.00, 1.00] (substantial)
#> • krippendorff_alpha: 0.80 [-0.00, 1.00] (substantial)
#> • gwet_ac1: 0.82 [0.45, 1.00] (almost perfect)
#> 1 disagreement; inspect `confusion_metrics()` before use.
#> ℹ No deployment decision is implied; call report() with a policy to assess one.
